week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers train as kindness superheroes—helpers who carry, comfort, and care. They try soft capes and badges, complete short training courses, rescue stuffed animals, pack helper kits, and build a blanket headquarters. Fighting and weapon play are redirected to helping jobs. Friday is a warm celebration of kindness (not a high-pressure graduation). Teachers should expect parallel play, brief attention, and repetition with help, gentle, brave, mission, and friend words.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice kindness, helping, turn-taking, and gentle touch with peers and props.
Language: Hear and try helper words such as kind, help, gentle, brave, rescue, mission, and thank you.
Cognitive: Follow simple mission sequences and match helper photos to props.
Fine motor: Stick badges, press play dough, and scoop sensory materials.
Gross motor: Crawl, balance on floor paths, carry deliveries, and parade.
Sensory: Explore dough, heart bins, and calm mission-prep textures.
Creative: Process masks/bands, helping-hands mural, and celebration medals.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: blocks, boxes, blankets/chairs for HQ, baskets, painter’s tape, smocks, towels, scarves
Hero props: soft breakaway capes, fabric cuffs, large badges, cardboard medals
Art: washable paint, paper masks/bands, stickers, stampers, glue sticks, mural paper
Sensory: play dough, foam hearts/stars, scoops, dry filler for kit packing
Dramatic play: stuffed animals, toy vehicles, mailbag, toy stethoscope (small parts removed)
Literacy: Kindness Is My Superpower; Even Superheroes Have Bad Days; How Kind!; Superheroes Are Everywhere; optional Be Kind (shortened)
Optional printables: picture kindness mission cards; helper zone signs
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: remove weapon toys; check capes for breakaway fasteners.
Prep picture kindness mission cards (no worksheets).
Stage blanket HQ and floor-level training course.
Choose 2–3 kindness/helper books (avoid fight-heavy plots).
Allergy-check dough/sensory fillers.
Plan Friday as a celebration circle with medals/stickers for everyone.
prepChecklist: Remove toy weapons and fighting props
Stage HQ blanket fort and training course
week.observationFocus:
Gentle vs rough touch with support
Kindness vocabulary attempts
Turn-taking on courses and bins
Redirectability from fight themes to helping
Sensory preferences
Comfort in celebration circle
week.familyConnection: Invite families to notice a community helper on the way home or practice one kind act together (hold a door, share a toy) and name it with a helper word. Optional: send a photo of a homemade paper badge—no homework required.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry to fort/course, no-paint art options, shorter missions, and picture supports. Never force costumes, hugs, or sharing.

activities.title: Design Your Superhero Identity
activities.objective: Explore soft hero props—capes, cuffs, and badges—so toddlers can choose what makes them feel like a helper hero for the week.
activities.description: Toddlers browse a basket of soft capes, fabric cuffs, and large helper badges. They may try one prop with help, look in a mirror, and hear kindness-hero words: help, gentle, brave, friend.
activities.materials:
3–4 soft toddler capes (velcro/breakaway, no ties around neck)
Fabric wrist cuffs
Large helper badges
Child-safe mirror
Basket
activities.preparation:
Check capes for breakaway fasteners
Remove masks with small elastic if unsafe—save decorating for later with paper masks
Sanitize props
activities.setup: Rug station with mirror and open basket. Space for 2–3 toddlers.
activities.steps:
1. Greet the helper basket.
2. Model putting on a cape with help.
3. Invite each child to choose one prop.
4. Look in the mirror together—wave hello, helper!
5. Practice a gentle “hero hands” open-palm gesture.
6. Rest props in the basket.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Which helper cape do you like?
Hero hands are gentle.
Do you see you in the mirror?
Brave and kind!
Cape off—rest time.
activities.observationOpportunities: Costume comfort, choice-making, mirror interest, and response to kindness language.
activities.safetyNotes: Capes breakaway only; never tie around necks. No real weapons or fighting props. Supervise mirrors. Soft props only.
activities.cleanupTips: Hang capes; badges in bin; wipe mirror.

observationPrompts: Which parts did the child attempt?
activities.adaptations: Hand-held support. Walking beside instead of crawling.
activities.extensions: Deliver a soft “aid kit” bag to the finish.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older add a hoop; younger crawl only.
activities.title: Superhero Training Obstacle Course
activities.objective: Move through a short helper-training course—crawl, step, and balance—to build coordination while practicing start/stop listening.
activities.description: Toddlers complete 3–4 low obstacles themed as hero training: crawl through a tunnel, step over soft noodles, walk a floor tape path, and freeze for “helper ready.”
activities.materials:
Play tunnel or chair tunnel
Pool noodles / soft blocks
Painter’s tape path
Finish cushion
Optional cape for the runner (optional)
activities.preparation:
Build low course
Spot-check spacing
No elevated climbs
activities.setup: One-way course with a teacher spotter. Waiting Xs on the floor.
activities.steps:
1. Model the course slowly.
2. Invite one toddler at a time.
3. Cheer effort, not speed.
4. Freeze pose at the finish—“Helper ready!”
5. Return along a side path.
6. Repeat short turns.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Crawl, hero!
Step carefully.
Walk the path.
Freeze—helper ready!
You trained hard!
activities.observationOpportunities: Motor planning, listening to cues, waiting, and confidence after tries.
activities.safetyNotes: Floor-level elements. Spot continuously. No racing or tackling. Capes optional and breakaway.

teacherTips: Display on a wall if children resist face wear.

substitutions.use: Paper plates as shield badges instead

activities.imageBriefExample: Process-art paper hero mask or forehead band with large stickers on an art tray. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.adaptations: Stickers-only tray. Pre-place one sticker to start.
activities.extensions: Add a large foam lightning or heart sticker as a kindness symbol.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older cut scrap shapes; toddlers stick.
activities.title: Hero Mask Decorating
activities.objective: Decorate paper hero masks with large stickers and stamps as process art—masks for pretend play display, not tight face-wear requirements.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate pre-cut paper half-masks or forehead hero bands with stickers, daubers, and crayons. Emphasize creating; wearing is optional and loosely fitted only.
activities.materials:
Pre-cut paper masks OR forehead bands (prefer bands for under-2)
Large stickers, daubers, crayons
Glue sticks
Smocks
Optional short yarn ties ONLY if adult-supervised and easily removable—prefer stick-on foam bands
activities.preparation:
Pre-cut shapes with large eye holes if using masks
Prefer headbands without covering eyes for 12–18 months
Portion stickers
activities.setup: Art table for 2–3. One mask/band each.
activities.steps:
1. Show a blank mask/band.
2. Invite stickers and color marks.
3. Process decorate freely.
4. Teacher adds name on the back.
5. Optional gentle try-on or display on a hook.
6. Dry if painted.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Which sticker for your hero mask?
Dab the color!
More or all done?
Shall we try it gently?
Your helper look shines!
activities.observationOpportunities: Fine-motor sticking, choice, and comfort with face-near props.
activities.safetyNotes: Prefer forehead bands over eye-covering masks for young toddlers. No small gems. Never force wearing. Elastic must be loose/breakaway if used.

teacherTips: One tool type at a time reduces overwhelm.

substitutions.use: Covered LED tea lights in jars

observationPrompts: Did the child point light safely?
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Shadow play with flashlights in a shaded nook (still eye-safe).

activities.extensions: Make a shadow puppet with a hand shape on the wall.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older name helpers; younger feel textures.

activities.title: Superhero Discovery Station
activities.objective: Investigate helper tools and materials—flashlights, fabric textures, and large magnets—to notice cause/effect in a toddler-safe discovery tray.
activities.description: Toddlers explore a discovery station with battery flashlights (eye-safe habits), fabric “cape” textures, large Magnatiles or magnetic wands with chunky metal lids, and helper picture cards.
activities.materials:
Battery flashlights (toddler-safe)
Fabric squares (shiny, soft, bumpy)
Large magnetic tiles or chunky magnetic wand + large metal lids
Helper photo cards (firefighter, nurse, teacher—kindness focus)
Tray
activities.preparation:
Test flashlights; remove cracked lenses
Cull small magnet pieces
Stage cards
activities.setup: Low table tray for 2 toddlers. Model flashlight pointed at floor/wall only.
activities.steps:
1. Show flashlight on floor—never in eyes.
2. Feel fabric textures; which feels like a cape?
3. Stick magnetic lids / tiles together.
4. Match a helper card to a prop if interested.
5. Free explore with narration.
6. Lights off; props rest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Point the light at the floor.
Soft or bumpy?
Stick, stick—together!
Who is this helper?
Discovery all done.
activities.observationOpportunities: Curiosity, flashlight safety with support, texture preferences, and magnetic cause/effect.
activities.safetyNotes: Never shine lights in eyes. Magnets large only—no swallowed magnet risk pieces. Battery compartments secured. Supervise closely.
activities.cleanupTips: Flashlights off; sort textures; secure magnets.

teacherTips: Prefer kindness books over fight scenes.
observationPrompts: Did the child point to a helper?
activities.adaptations: Standing listeners OK. Single picture card story.
activities.extensions: Act out one kind act with puppets after.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older turn pages; younger point.
activities.title: Hero Story Circle
activities.objective: Share a short kindness/helper story and invite toddlers to point, name feelings, and connect helpers to classroom hero play.
activities.description: Small-group read-aloud of a kindness or gentle superhero book with pointing and short feeling questions. Toddlers may hold a soft cape scrap while listening.
activities.materials:
Kindness/helper book (e.g., Kindness Is My Superpower; Even Superheroes Have Bad Days; How Kind!; Superheroes Are Everywhere)
Soft cape scrap or badge
Cushions
activities.preparation:
Preview length; pick 2–3 talk pages
Stage prop

activities.steps:
1. Show the cover—who is the helper?
2. Read briefly with pointing.
3. Ask a feeling question.
4. Invite a gentle hero-hands gesture.
5. Picture-walk a favorite page again.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who is helping?
How does the friend feel?
What is kind?

activities.observationOpportunities: Attention, pointing, feeling words, and connection to kindness theme.

teacherTips: Keep tone warm; avoid scary “danger” talk.

activities.title: Rescue the Animals Mission
activities.objective: Rescue stuffed animals with gentle carrying and soft wraps, practicing caregiving hero roles without fighting or fear themes.
activities.description: Toddlers find soft animals needing help and carry them to a rescue mat, offering a blanket and pretend check. Mission language stays calm: help, gentle, safe, thank you.
activities.materials:
4–5 stuffed animals
Rescue mat or basket
Soft blankets
Optional toy stethoscope (no small parts)
Helper badges
activities.preparation:
Sanitize animals
Stage “need help” spots
Remove any weapon props nearby
activities.setup: Scattered animals + central rescue mat. Clear paths.
activities.steps:
1. Notice an animal—“Needs a helper!”
2. Model gentle pick-up and wrap.
3. Carry to the rescue mat.
4. Listen/pretend check briefly.
5. Rest animal safely.
6. Cheer “All friends safe!”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who can help?
Gentle hands.
Wrap the friend.
Safe on the mat.
Thank you, hero!
activities.observationOpportunities: Gentle touch, empathy, carrying, and mission completion.
activities.safetyNotes: Large soft animals. No tossing. Paths clear. Caregiving—not combat—framing only.

substitutions.use: A soft stuffed toy to carry

observationPrompts: Did the child complete a delivery?
activities.adaptations: Push a cart instead of carrying. Shorter path.
activities.extensions: Two-item delivery for children ready for more.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older pack bags; younger deliver.
activities.title: Carry and Deliver Challenge
activities.objective: Carry soft “supply” bags along a short path and deliver them to a helper station, building balance, persistence, and helping vocabulary.
activities.description: Toddlers carry lightweight bags or baskets with soft scarves/beans bags from a start line to a delivery table, practicing careful walking and handoff.
activities.materials:
Soft tote bags or baskets
Scarf “supplies” or large beanbags
Delivery table/box labeled with a heart picture
Tape path
activities.preparation:
Pack light bags
Clear path
Mark start and delivery
activities.setup: Short path for one carrier at a time. Teacher at delivery for handoff.
activities.steps:
1. Show the heart delivery box.
2. Model careful carry.
3. Invite a toddler to walk the path.
4. Deliver and say “For you!”
5. Return empty-handed along the side.
6. Repeat turns.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Carry carefully!
Walking feet.
Deliver to the heart.
For you—thank you!
Ready for another delivery?
activities.observationOpportunities: Bilateral carry, path staying, handoff social moment, and waiting.
activities.safetyNotes: Bags light. No running. Floor clear. Beanbags large. Spot balance.

teacherTips: Keep road one-way to reduce crashes.
observationPrompts: Did the child push a vehicle to the mat?
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Wagon decorating as a rescue vehicle outdoors.
activities.adaptations: Pre-built base to decorate. Hand-under-hand push.
activities.extensions: Try which vehicle slides farther with a gentle push.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older tape wheels; toddlers push.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Block and box rescue vehicles on a tape road toward a rescue mat. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Build a Rescue Vehicle
activities.objective: Build simple rescue vehicles from blocks and boxes to explore wheels, pushing, and pretend helping transport.
activities.description: Toddlers stack boxes/blocks into ambulances, boats, or helper cars and push them along a tape road to a rescue mat, loading soft animals if desired.
activities.materials:
Blocks, small boxes, plate “wheels”
Tape road
Soft animals optional
Rescue mat destination
Tape/glue dots for teacher-secure wheels
activities.preparation:
Sort large parts
Lay road tape
Pre-make 1 sample vehicle
activities.setup: Build table beside road. Limit 3 builders.
activities.steps:
1. Show a simple block vehicle.
2. Invite stacking a cabin on a base.
3. Add wheels with help if needed.
4. Push along the road to the mat.
5. Load a friend animal (optional).
6. Rebuild after tip-overs cheerfully.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What is your rescue ride?
Stack the cabin.
Need wheels?
Push to the rescue mat!
Helping vehicle go!
activities.observationOpportunities: Stacking, pushing control, pretend rescue language, and persistence.
activities.safetyNotes: Large parts only. Teacher secures loose wheels. No small axles. Supervise mouthing.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort blocks; roll tape if needed.

teacherTips: Offer cool dough for seekers of strong input.

substitutions.use: Cloud dough or kinetic sand with large molds

observationPrompts: How did the child respond to dough texture?
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Play dough outdoors for easier crumb control.

activities.extensions: Press dough onto a cardboard badge and take-home (if dry policy allows).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older combine colors; toddlers pinch only.

activities.title: Superhero Play Dough Creations
activities.objective: Press, pinch, and stamp play dough to make open-ended hero shapes, badges, and snakes—focusing on hand strength and sensory comfort.
activities.description: Toddlers explore play dough with large cookie cutters (stars, hearts, circles), rollers, and craft sticks to create badges and free forms. No required finished character.
activities.materials:
Play dough (allergy-aware; homemade or commercial)
Large heart/star cutters
Rollers, craft sticks
Placemats, wipes
Optional glitter-free “cape” fabric scrap to press textures
activities.preparation:
Allergy check (wheat dough alternatives ready)
Portion dough balls
Set wipe station
activities.setup: Table for 2–3. One dough ball each. Tools in a caddy.
activities.steps:
1. Warm dough in hands together.
2. Squish, pinch, roll snakes.
3. Press a heart/star badge.
4. Add texture with fabric if desired.
5. Squish to reset—process OK.
6. Store dough; wipe hands/table.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Squish, squish!
Can you roll a snake?
Heart badge press!
All done squishing?
Strong helper hands!
activities.observationOpportunities: Hand strength, sensory tolerance, tool use, and creativity without product pressure.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise mouthing. Allergy alternatives. Tools large. No tiny beads mixed in.
activities.cleanupTips: Seal dough; wash tools; wipe table.

activities.adaptations: Lap bouncing for infants/young toddlers with caregiver.
activities.extensions: Let a child pick the next cue card.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older lead cues; younger approximate.
activities.title: Hero Movement Dance
activities.objective: Dance with hero poses—reach high, march, and freeze—to build listening, balance, and joyful movement tied to helping themes.
activities.description: Toddlers move to short music tracks with cues: fly arms (gentle), march feet, heart-hands, and freeze helper poses. No tackling or combat moves.
activities.materials:
Open floor
Music player (soft)
Optional scarves
Picture cue cards (fly, march, heart, freeze)
activities.preparation:
Clear space
Choose 2 short songs
Prep cue cards
activities.setup: Circle or scattered spots with space between children.
activities.steps:
1. Show fly arms—soft, not bumping.
2. Start music; march.
3. Heart-hands on chest.
4. Freeze helper pose.
5. Scarf wave round.
6. Rest seated.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Fly gently!
March, march!
Heart hands—kind!
Freeze, helper!
Rest your powers.
activities.observationOpportunities: Imitation, freeze listening, spatial awareness, and enjoyment.
activities.safetyNotes: Space out. No flying into peers. No kick/punch cues. Soft volume.

observationPrompts: Did the child choose a card?
Did they attempt the kind act?
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Outdoor kindness tidy mission (collect soft toys).
activities.adaptations: Teacher chooses; child acts. One-card session.
activities.extensions: Send a duplicate picture card home for family kindness play.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older describe the card; toddlers point and act.

activities.title: Kindness Mission Cards

activities.description: Toddlers sit briefly, look at large picture cards (share toy, gentle pat, help tidy), choose one, and try the kind act with props. Cards are visual only—no tracing or word worksheets.
activities.materials:
Large picture mission cards (photos/icons)
Props: toys to share, soft doll, tidy bin
Cushions
Optional pocket chart to display cards
activities.preparation:
Print/laminate 4–5 picture cards
Stage props
Plan 2–3 missions max for attention
activities.setup: Half-group circle. Cards face out. Props nearby.
activities.steps:
1. Show two cards and name the helps.
2. Invite a child to point/choose.
3. Act out the mission with a prop or peer (with consent).
4. Cheer the kind act.
5. Choose another card.
6. Close with “Kindness heroes!”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Which kindness mission?
Share the toy?
Gentle pat?
Help tidy—drop in the bin!
You were kind!

substitutions.use: Stamp pads with large hand stampers

observationPrompts: Did they place a hand on the mural?

activities.extensions: Walk to the window and look for a helper vehicle (if safe/visible).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older name helpers; younger try hats.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Community helper investigation table with soft hats, mailbag, stethoscope, and photo cards. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Community Helper Investigation
activities.objective: Investigate real community helper tools and photos—hats, bags, and gentle instruments—to notice who helps in our neighborhood.
activities.description: Toddlers explore a helper investigation table with oversized hats (firefighter/nurse dress-up soft versions), a toy medical kit with small parts removed, mailbag, and photo cards of real helpers.
activities.materials:
Soft helper hats
Mailbag with large envelopes
Toy stethoscope
Photo cards of community helpers
Clipboard with big photos (no writing required)
activities.preparation:
Remove tiny kit pieces
Sanitize hats
Select 3–4 helper photos
activities.setup: Investigation table for 2–3. Clear labels with pictures.
activities.steps:
1. Show a helper photo—who is this?
2. Match a prop to the photo.
3. Try the mailbag delivery to a chair “mailbox.”
4. Listen with stethoscope on a stuffed friend.
5. Free explore with narration.
6. Hats rest on hooks.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who helps us?
Firefighter hat?
Mail for the mailbox!
Listen—heartbeat?
Helpers are kind!
activities.observationOpportunities: Matching photos to props, pretend helping, curiosity, and vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: No real tools/weapons. Soft hats. Kit pieces large only. Stethoscope cords short/supervised.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort props by helper type; hang hats.

teacherTips: Offer alternative: “Helpers carry, they don’t hit.”

substitutions.use: Any cars + red cross heart sticker

activities.adaptations: One-step job cards. Parallel play OK.
activities.extensions: Add a hospital block building for resting friends.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older build towers; toddlers drive and deliver.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Block city with toy vehicles, soft figures, and a heart safe-zone mat. Kindness focus. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: City Rescue Adventure
activities.objective: Act out a calm city helping adventure with block buildings, rescue vehicles, and caregiving roles—helping neighbors, not battling villains.
activities.description: Toddlers use blocks as city buildings, push rescue vehicles, and help soft people/animals to a safe zone. Teacher narrates kindness missions; no punching or weapon play.
activities.materials:
Blocks for buildings
Toy vehicles (ambulance/fire—or generic cars)
Soft people/animals
Safe-zone mat with heart sign
Capes optional
activities.preparation:
Build a simple block city starter
Stage safe zone
Remove fighting toys
activities.setup: City rug: buildings, road, safe zone. Limit 3–4 players.
activities.steps:
1. Tour the city and safe heart zone.
2. Model helping a soft friend to safety.
3. Push a vehicle along the road.
4. Deliver helper supplies (scarves).
5. Rotate roles: driver, helper, friend.
6. Close city—everyone safe.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who needs help in our city?
Drive carefully.
To the safe heart!
Thank you, helper.
City is calm and kind.
activities.observationOpportunities: Pretend sequences, gentle themes, vehicle control, and peer roles.
activities.safetyNotes: Redirect any hit/kick play to helping jobs. Soft props. Clear roads. No weapon toys.
activities.cleanupTips: Blocks sorted; vehicles parked; friends in basket.

teacherTips: Keep HQ calm—not a wrestle zone.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Table fort if chairs are limited.
activities.adaptations: Sit beside HQ first. Shorter blanket cave.
activities.extensions: Add a mailbox for kindness notes (scribbles OK).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older clip blankets; toddlers cushion and play.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Blanket-chair helper headquarters with cushions, badges, and a picture mission board. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Build a Superhero Headquarters
activities.objective: Build a helper headquarters from blankets, chairs, and blocks where toddlers can gather props and plan kind missions.
activities.description: Toddlers drape blankets over chairs to make a HQ fort, place badges and flashlights inside, and use it as a calm base between pretend missions.
activities.materials:
Chairs/clips + blanket
Cushions inside
Badge basket
Flashlight
Picture mission board (heart icons)
activities.preparation:
Stable fort frame
Test clips
Remove tip hazards
activities.setup: HQ in a corner with open entry. Max 2–3 inside.
activities.steps:
1. Help drape the blanket with teacher.
2. Add cushions.
3. Place badges inside.
4. Sit in HQ and choose a picture mission.
5. Go do the mission; return to HQ.
6. Rest powers in the fort.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Build our helper HQ!
Cushions in.
Badges ready.
What mission picture?
Back to headquarters—rest.
activities.observationOpportunities: Cooperative building, comfort in cozy spaces, and mission choice.
activities.safetyNotes: Fort stable; adult checks. No heavy objects overhead. Flashlight eye-safe. Ventilation/open side.
activities.cleanupTips: Fold blanket; return chairs; badges to bin.

teacherTips: Drop-in counts as success for young toddlers.
activities.adaptations: Omit crawl. Hand-held plank walk.
activities.extensions: Carry a badge through the whole course.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toss; younger drop.
activities.title: Hero Training Course
activities.objective: Complete a varied hero training course with climbing-under, balancing, and delivery to reinforce whole-body control and helping end goals.
activities.description: Toddlers crawl under a bench, walk a floor beam/tape, toss a soft beanbag into a heart bin (underhand), and finish with a helper pose.
activities.materials:
Bench/table crawl
Floor plank or tape
Soft beanbags
Heart bin target
Finish mat
activities.preparation:
Set low crawl space
Plank on floor only
Spot toss zone
activities.setup: Linear course; one child moving; teacher spots plank and toss.
activities.steps:
1. Model each station.
2. Crawl under.
3. Walk the plank path.
4. Underhand toss to heart bin (or drop in).
5. Helper pose finish.
6. Side-path return.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Crawl under!
Balance steps.
Drop or toss gently.
Helper pose!
Training done!
activities.observationOpportunities: Motor variety, aim attempt, listening, and celebration of effort.
activities.safetyNotes: Plank floor-level. Underhand only—no hard throws at people. Spot continuously.

teacherTips: Child-chosen “power” can be a gesture if words are few.
observationPrompts: Did the child wear the badge?
activities.imageBriefExample: Toddler-decorated helper badge with large stickers on a cardboard circle. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.adaptations: One sticker badge. Teacher holds while child sticks.
activities.extensions: Photo of badge for portfolio.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older write a letter; toddlers scribble/stick.
activities.title: Super Badge Creation
activities.objective: Create wearable helper badges with stickers and drawing on large circles—process identity art celebrating kindness powers.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate cardboard circle badges with stickers, stamps, and scribbles, then wear them with painter’s tape or a large safety-safe clip managed by adults.
activities.materials:
Cardboard circles / pre-cut badge shapes
Stickers, stampers, crayons
Painter’s tape or badge clips (adult-applied)
Smocks optional
activities.preparation:
Pre-cut circles
Portion stickers
Prep tape pieces
activities.setup: Art table for 2–3. One badge each.
activities.steps:
1. Show a blank badge.
2. Decorate with stickers/scribbles.
3. Name a kindness power together (helps, hugs, shares)—teacher may write a word.
4. Adult tapes badge to shirt.
5. Mirror look optional.
6. Wear for HQ play.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Decorate your badge!
What is your kind power?
Sticker here?
Badge on—helper ready!
You look proud!
activities.observationOpportunities: Fine motor, identity language, and pride wearing badge.
activities.safetyNotes: Adult applies tape/clips. No pins. Large stickers. Supervise mouthing of cardboard.
activities.cleanupTips: Extra badges flat to dry; wipe table.

observationPrompts: Did the child pack an item?
activities.adaptations: Pre-packed kit to unpack only. Larger scoops.
activities.extensions: Deliver kit to a stuffed friend at HQ.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older pack full kits; younger scoop only.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Sensory tub with scoops, fabric bandages, and a helper kit box. Calm prep theme. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Emergency Mission Sensory Play
activities.objective: Explore a calm “mission prep” sensory bin with scoops of beans/rice, cups, and first-aid soft props to practice filling helper kits.
activities.description: Toddlers scoop dry filler into cups and bags to pack a pretend helper kit with large bandages (fabric) and soft gauze, keeping the mood steady and helpful—not scary.
activities.materials:
Sensory tub + dry filler (oats/rice/paper)
Cups, scoops, small bags
Large fabric bandages
Soft gauze strips
Kit box
Smocks
activities.preparation:
Allergy check
Portion filler
Cull small parts
activities.setup: Tub for 2. Kit box at the side for packed items.
activities.steps:
1. Scoop filler into a cup—“supplies!”
2. Pack a fabric bandage in the kit.
3. Add a soft gauze strip.
4. Close kit and carry to HQ mat.
5. Unpack and repeat if interested.
6. Sweep help.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Pack the helper kit.
Scoop supplies.
Bandage in.
Kit ready!
Calm helpers prepare.
activities.observationOpportunities: Scooping, sequencing pack steps, sensory comfort, and calm engagement.
activities.safetyNotes: Frame as practice helping—not real emergencies/fear. Large props. Supervise mouthing. No real meds.
activities.cleanupTips: Empty kits; store filler; wash hands.

activities.adaptations: Wagon riders shake bells.
activities.extensions: Show mural hands mid-parade.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older lead; infants bounce.
activities.title: Hero Parade
activities.objective: Parade with badges and scarves to music, celebrating helper identities and group joy at week’s end.
activities.description: Toddlers wear badges/capes if desired and march a loop waving scarves, pausing for a group “helpers hooray!” cheer.
activities.materials:
Badges/capes optional
Scarves
Music
Parade loop markers
activities.preparation:
Clear loop
Stage props
Choose upbeat short track
activities.setup: Start on rug; teacher leads; space marchers.
activities.steps:
1. Optional costume on.
2. March to music.
3. Wave scarves.
4. Pause—helpers hooray!
5. One more loop.
6. Bow and rest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Heroes ready?
March and wave!
Helpers hooray!
What a team!
Rest your feet.
activities.observationOpportunities: Group movement, prop comfort, and celebration participation.
activities.safetyNotes: Space out. No running. Scarves not on necks. Soft volume.

teacherTips: Jobs can be tiny for young toddlers.
observationPrompts: Did the child help tidy or deliver?
activities.adaptations: One job only. Picture job cards.
activities.extensions: Invite a visitor to see the saved city.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older rebuild; younger deliver scarves.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddlers’ block city tidy/rescue scene with heart safe mat and soft friends. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Save the City Challenge
activities.objective: Complete a final cooperative challenge: tidy the block city, deliver supplies, and settle friends in the safe zone—celebration through helping work.
activities.description: Toddlers work together to reset the block city, deliver scarf supplies, and place soft friends on the heart mat. Framed as saving the day by caring, not fighting.
activities.materials:
Block city pieces
Soft friends
Supply scarves
Heart safe mat
Timer optional (visual sand timer)
activities.preparation:
Messy-ish city setup ready to reset
Stage supplies
Review kindness language
activities.setup: City rug with clear jobs: tidy, deliver, settle.
activities.steps:
1. Look at the messy city—helpers needed!
2. Tidy blocks into a bin or rebuild simply.
3. Deliver scarves to the safe mat.
4. Settle soft friends.
5. Group cheer: city saved by kindness!
6. Photo/memory optional.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Helpers save the day by caring!
Tidy a block?
Deliver supplies.
Friends on the heart.
City saved—kindness wins!
activities.observationOpportunities: Cooperation, tidy persistence, and understanding of helping as “saving.”
activities.safetyNotes: Redirect combat themes. Soft landings for blocks. Clear walking space.
activities.cleanupTips: This activity IS cleanup—finish with labeled bins.

teacherTips: Every child gets a medal—no ranking.
Recall real moments (“you shared a scarf”).
activities.imageBriefExample: Toddler hero medal craft with stickers and ribbon, celebration focus. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.adaptations: Stickers only; adult finishes.
activities.extensions: Family note on the back with a kindness memory.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older color longer; toddlers sticker.
activities.title: Create a Hero Medal
activities.objective: Make process-art hero medals to celebrate kindness efforts—wearable keepsakes without ranking or competition.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate large cardboard medals with stickers, yarn (adult-tied loosely or taped), and stamps. Every child receives celebration recognition for helping tries.
activities.materials:
Cardboard medal circles
Stickers, stamps, crayons
Yarn or ribbon (adult-managed, breakaway/tape preferred)
Hole punch (adult)
activities.preparation:
Pre-cut medals; pre-punch holes
Prep yarn lengths
Portion stickers
activities.setup: Art table for 2–3. Adult station for yarn.
activities.steps:
1. Decorate medal freely.
2. Adult adds yarn/tape loop.
3. Name one kind thing the child did this week (teacher may recall).
4. Place medal on child or in cubby.
5. Mirror moment optional.
6. Group smile.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Decorate your medal!
You helped this week.
Medal for kindness!
Wear or keep in cubby?
Proud helper!
activities.observationOpportunities: Art engagement and response to specific kindness recognition.
activities.safetyNotes: Adult manages yarn—no long neck loops unattended. Prefer tape-on shirts for under-2. Large stickers.

activities.adaptations: Surface finds for easy success.
activities.extensions: Count stars with pointing cheers.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older hide; younger find.
activities.imageBriefSetup: Celebration sensory bin with large stars/hearts and scoops. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.title: Superhero Sensory Celebration
activities.objective: Celebrate with a festive sensory bin of large star/heart fillers and scoops, enjoying textures and shared discovery.
activities.description: Toddlers dig in a celebration bin with star foam, fabric scraps, and hidden badges, cheering finds in a calm festive tone.
activities.materials:
Sensory tub
Large star/heart foam
Fabric scraps
Hidden badge pieces (large)
Scoops
Smocks
activities.preparation:
Bury a few large surprises
Allergy check
Set celebration music soft optional
activities.setup: Bin for 2–3. Festive but calm.
activities.steps:
1. Announce sensory celebration.
2. Scoop and dig.
3. Share finds on a tray.
4. Notice textures.
5. Re-hide for a friend.
6. Wave bye to the bin.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Celebration dig!
Star for you!
Share the tray.
Soft or bumpy?
What a hero week!
activities.observationOpportunities: Sensory joy, sharing, and week-end wind-down engagement.
activities.safetyNotes: Large fillers. Supervise mouthing. Avoid overstimulation—limit time.

teacherTips: Say celebration more than graduation if families worry about pressure.
Skip diplomas that require long sitting.
activities.decisionNote: Priority 1 rewrite; reframed as celebration not formal graduation
activities.adaptations: Lap sitting or edge standing OK. Watching counts.
activities.extensions: Family join for the cheer if pickup aligns.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older help pass stickers; toddlers receive.
activities.title: Junior Hero Graduation Ceremony
activities.objective: Celebrate the week’s helper heroes with a song, optional medal show, and kindness cheer—framed as a warm celebration gathering, not a formal test or performance pressure.
activities.description: Toddlers gather for a short celebration: sing a helper chant, optionally show a badge/medal, receive a sticker, and hear specific kindness memories. Keep it brief, joyful, and optional for showing.
activities.materials:
Cushions
Medals/badges
Celebration stickers
Song card
Optional photo prop
activities.preparation:
Prep stickers
Recall 1 kindness moment per child if possible
Choose 1 short song
activities.setup: Circle whole or half group. Under 10 minutes.
activities.steps:
1. Welcome helper heroes with a wave.
2. Sing one kindness chant.
3. Optional show-and-share of medal/badge.
4. Teacher names class helps from the week.
5. Sticker for each child.
6. Cheer “Kind heroes forever!” and dismiss to play.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Welcome, helpers!
You were kind this week.
Show your medal if you like.
Sticker celebration!
Kind heroes forever!
activities.observationOpportunities: Circle comfort, pride responses, and engagement with celebration language.
activities.safetyNotes: No forcing performance. Stickers large. Keep short. Calling it celebration reduces graduation pressure.
